bill.title: To improve the Indian School Equalization Formula and Indian School Equalization Program of the Bureau of Indian Education, and for other purposes.
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the House Committee on Education and Workforce.

classification.plainSummary: This bill would revise the funding formula and program used by the Bureau of Indian Education to allocate resources to schools serving Native American students. It aims to improve how federal education dollars are distributed to Bureau-operated and tribally controlled schools. The bill addresses equity and adequacy in funding for schools on or near Indian reservations.

industries.rationale: The bill directly changes funding formulas and program operations for Bureau of Indian Education schools and education services.
The bill modifies how a federal agency (Bureau of Indian Education) administers its school funding program and allocates resources.

method.formula: score = Σ_industries ( donorShare(industry) × billWeight(industry) ), where billWeight = classifierConfidence / Σ classifierConfidence. Range 0–1, read as a weighted share of disclosed itemized money.

ordinary.text: They wrote this bill. Sponsoring a bill about your own district's industry is the ordinary case, not the odd one.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
